First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f = \cosh g, \qquad g = \sqrt x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\dfrac {\textrm{d}f} {\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac {\textrm{d}f} {\textrm{d}g} \cdot \dfrac {\textrm{d}g} {\textrm{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\dfrac {\textrm{d}f} {\textrm{d}g}  = \sinh g,
$$

and

$$
\dfrac {\textrm{d}g} {\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt x}.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡g\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡\sqrt{x}}{2\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$
